content: 1. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor and should not be co-administered with sensitive CYP3A substrates, as it can increase the levels or effects of drugs like cobicistat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 2. Cobicistat can decrease the levels or effects of ifosfamide by affecting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Similarly, atazanavir can also reduce the efficacy of ifosfamide by altering its metabolism, necessitating therapy adjustments and close monitoring. 3. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active metabolites, potentially decreasing its efficacy. Close monitoring is advised. 4. Atazanavir can increase the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone itself can increase atazanavir levels. Caution and close monitoring are required, as iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor that may elevate plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. 5. Cobicistat and atazanavir can increase the levels or effects of imatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor but should still be monitored closely. 6. Atazanavir increases the levels of imipramine through an unspecified mechanism and by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases imipramine levels. Caution is advised, and antidepressant doses should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect. 7. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of indinavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with cobicistat and atazanavir is contraindicated due to the risk of indirect hyperbilirubinemia and immune reconstitution syndrome. 8. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of irinotecan and its liposomal formulation by decreasing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated, as UGT1A1 inhibitors further reduce irinotecan metabolism. 9. Isavuconazonium sulfate levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir through CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of isradipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor but should be monitored closely. 12. Istradefylline increases the levels of cobicistat and atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The dose of istradefylline should not exceed 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and atazanavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 14. Ivabradine levels are significantly increased by cobicistat and atazanavir through CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Ivacaftor levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Ivosidenib levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided, or the ivosidenib dose should be reduced to 250 mg daily. 17. Ixabepilone levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir through CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 18. Monitoring is still recommended. 19. Ketamine levels are decreased by atazanavir through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 21. Labetalol effects are increased by atazanavir through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, and AV block. Beta-blocker doses may need to be reduced. 22. Lacosamide levels are increased by atazanavir and cobicistat through CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Lamivudine and atazanavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Close monitoring is required. 24. Lamotrigine levels are decreased by atazanavir, especially when boosted with ritonavir. Close monitoring is necessary. 25. Lansoprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility and plasma concentrations. Co-administration should be avoided. 26. Lapatinib levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. If co-administration is unavoidable, the lapatinib dose should be adjusted. 27. Larotrectinib levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 28. Lefamulin levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. 29. Lemborexant levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. 30. Lenacapavir levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration with atazanavir/cobicistat or atazanavir/ritonavir should be avoided. 31. Leniolisib levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 32. Letermovir levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Close monitoring is required. 33. Levamlodipine levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Dose adjustments and monitoring for hypotension and edema are recommended. 34. Levonorgestrel levels may be increased or decreased by atazanavir. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 35. Lidocaine levels are increased by cobicistat. Clinical monitoring is recommended during co-administration with antiarrhythmics. 36. Linagliptin levels are increased by atazanavir. Close monitoring is advised. 37. Liraglutide effects are decreased by atazanavir, potentially due to insulin resistance. Close monitoring is recommended. 38. Lofepramine levels are increased by atazanavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Lomitapide levels are significantly increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Lonafarnib levels are significantly increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Lopinavir levels are increased by atazanavir, and vice versa. Co-administration should be avoided. 42. Loratadine levels are increased by atazanavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Lorlatinib levels are decreased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration should be avoided, or the lorlatinib dose should be adjusted. 44. Losartan levels are increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Lovastatin levels are significantly increased by cobicistat and atazanavir. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
